title: History & Diffs
tagline: Every commit is a snapshot AND a diff -- Git stores the former, but almost always shows you the latter.

concept.label: What
concept.text: git log shows commit history; git diff shows exact line changes; git show shows one commit's full diff.

concept.label: Why
concept.text: "What changed, and why" is the single most common question in any real codebase -- these three commands answer it.

concept.label: How
concept.text: diff compares two states (working-vs-staged by default); pass commit hashes or branch names to compare anything to anything.

concept.label: When
concept.text: Before committing (review your own changes), or investigating when/why a bug was introduced.

concept.label: Where
concept.text: Code review (Module 7), and every debugging session that starts with "this used to work."

mnemonic.label: L.D.S.
mnemonic.text: Log (the list) -> Diff (the changes) -> Show (one commit's full story)

sandboxNote.text: run these in a repo with real history -- your Module 1-3 repo already has enough commits to be useful.

code:
git log                         # full history, newest first
git log --oneline               # LOG: compact, one line per commit -- use this daily
git log --oneline -5            # just the last 5 commits

echo "extra line" >> README.md
git diff                        # DIFF: unstaged changes, line by line (+/-)
git add README.md
git diff --staged               # DIFF: what's staged, about to be committed

git log --oneline               # find a commit hash from the list, then:
git show a1b2c3d                 # SHOW: that exact commit's full diff + message

cycle.title: Read the concept table once
cycle.text: Notice the pairing: log tells you WHEN and by WHOM; diff/show tell you WHAT actually changed, line by line. You'll reach for both together constantly.

cycle.title: Type the code yourself — no copy-paste
cycle.text: Make an edit, run git diff BEFORE staging, then git add and git diff --staged AFTER -- confirm the output moves from one command to the other as you'd expect.
cycle.hint: Red lines (removed) and green lines (added) in diff output map directly to what git add is about to snapshot. Reading a diff before every commit is a habit worth building now.

cycle.title: Apply it to your own data
cycle.text: Pick any commit from your own history with git log --oneline, copy its hash, and run git show on it -- read the real diff of something you actually wrote.

cycle.title: Reflect & note
cycle.text: Did reading your own diff before committing catch anything you didn't mean to include?
cycle.placeholder: e.g. git diff showed a debug print statement I'd forgotten to remove -- caught it before committing instead of after...

cycle.title: Tick off before moving on
checklist: I can explain the difference between git diff and git diff --staged.
I ran git log --oneline and read real history I created.
I ran git show on a real commit hash from my own history.
I caught something in a diff before committing it.
I wrote a reflection note above.
